title: BlueHarbor Health POC — Security Responses & Evidence
content:
Working draft: consolidated infosec Q&A and evidence index prepared for BlueHarbor Health POC.

Summary
- Purpose: Provide BlueHarbor with concise answers to their security questionnaire and a packaged list of evidence artifacts they requested for the hosted POC (data residency in us-east-1, encrypted at rest/in transit, redaction and minimal retention). This doc is intended for the BlueHarbor security team and our SE + SecOps reviewers.
- Status: in_review. Several evidence items pending legal approval (BAA markups) and updated pen-test upload (expect by 2026-02-14).

Scope of POC
- Duration: 8 weeks (pilot environment isolated per-customer within Redwood hosted cluster).
- Data type: de-identified PHI and test patient records; BlueHarbor will send hashed identifiers only for evaluation.
- Deployment mode: Hosted API with dedicated tenant isolation and per-customer S3 buckets. Option to move to Dedicated capacity if performance SLA required.

High-level answers to BlueHarbor questionnaire (condensed)
1) Data classification and flow\- All customer payloads are classified as customer data. For this POC we will treat BlueHarbor data as PHI under a BAA scope. Data flow: API ingress -> request router -> tenant worker -> ephemeral KV cache -> response. Logs scrubbed; request/response bodies not stored permanently unless customer opt-in for eval retention.

2) Encryption\- In transit: TLS1.2+ enforced with strong ciphers.\- At rest: Customer buckets encrypted with AWS KMS CMKs. Keys are customer-dedicated when requested (Bring Your Own Key supported for Dedicated/Private). Key rotation: annual by default; can configure quarterly.

3) Access control and IAM\- Principle of least privilege enforced.\- Admin access to production environment is role-based and recorded via short-lived AWS STS credentials.\- Privileged access requires 2FA and SSO via Okta.

4) Logging and monitoring\- Audit logs stored in tamper-evident S3 prefix, forwarded to our Splunk stack for 365-day retention standard (longer retention available as add-on).\- Kube audit logs, request traces, and token-level latency/cost metrics available per route in Console.

5) Incident response\- IR runbook exists; we will notify BlueHarbor within 24 hours of any confirmed data exposure. Support: dedicated SE on call for the POC. Post-incident review and root cause remediation planned with timelines.

6) Penetration testing and third-party assessment\- Most recent pentest: internal w/ third-party validation, report v2025-10 available. External full-scope pentest scheduled annually; adhoc tests require coordination. Findings tracked in JIRA-SEC (sample: SEC-2025-27).

7) Compliance posture\- Redwood: SOC2 Type II in scope (audit artifacts available under NDA).\- HIPAA: we operate under a BAA for customers requiring HIPAA controls; BAA draft shared with BlueHarbor legal.

8) Subprocessors and supply chain\- Cloud provider: AWS in us-east-1 for POC. Third-party vendors: Okta (SSO), Datadog (metrics), Sentry (error telemetry). Full subprocessors list attached as Evidence Item 02.

9) Data retention and deletion\- Default: 30 days of request metadata and 0 days of user request/response bodies unless retention consented. Deletion requests processed via Console or support ticket; data purge completes within 72 hours for POC environment.

10) Privacy and data minimization\- We recommend minimal request payloads for the POC. We will provide a redaction preprocessor to strip PII/PHI from prompts where needed.

11) Business continuity and backups\- Backups for infra state are performed nightly with encrypted snapshots. RTO/RPO targets for hosted POC: RTO 4 hours, RPO 1 hour for critical control plane components.

12) Auditability and evidence\- We will provide the following artifacts listed below. Some artifacts are restricted until NDA/BAA executed or after final sign-off.

Evidence index (packaged artifacts)\- Evidence 01: POC Data Flow Diagram (diagram.pdf) - annotated with per-step controls and S3 prefix names.\- Evidence 02: Subprocessor roster (subprocessors_2026-01.csv) - current as of 2026-01-20.\- Evidence 03: KMS key policy and CMK ARN examples (kms-policy-sample.txt).\- Evidence 04: PenTest summary and remediation tracker (pentest_summary_2025-10.txt). Full sensitive report available under NDA.\- Evidence 05: SOC2 Type II summary and auditor contact (soc2_summary_2024.pdf).\- Evidence 06: Sample audit log export and hash (auditlogs_sample_us-east-1.zip, sha256: abcdef...).\- Evidence 07: BAA draft (blueharbor_baa_v0.9.docx) - legal to review.\- Evidence 08: Console screenshots showing per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdown (console_route_traces.png).\- Evidence 09: Pen-test remediation tickets in JIRA (JIRA-SEC-2025-27, JIRA-SEC-2025-31).

Notes on evidence availability
- Items with sensitive details (full pen-test PDF, SOC2 auditor package) require executed NDA/BAA and secure artifact exchange.
- We can provide encrypted bundles via customer-secured S3 shares or a secure artifact exchange link.

Recommended POC deployment and controls (SE guidance)
- Start hosted POC in us-east-1 with per-customer isolation and BYOK disabled initially for speed.
- Toggle off request/response retention; enable only metadata collection for metrics.
- Enable pre-ingest redaction for PHI-sensitive prompt sets.
- If performance tests show tail latency issues, propose upgrade to small Dedicated pool for guaranteed throughput.

Workshop notes (internal meeting 2026-01-28 w/ BlueHarbor Sec + Product)
- Attendees: Marina (SE lead), Devon (SecOps), Priya (Solutions Eng), BlueHarbor: M. Alvarez (CISO), R. Chen (Platform).\- Main ask: confirm BAA terms and HIPAA control mappings against BlueHarbor ISMS.
- BlueHarbor requires a list of all subprocessors and encryption proof for S3 storage. Action: provide Evidence 02 and Evidence 03 by 2026-02-03.
- BlueHarbor wants the option to have dedicated keys; legal wants to verify key escrow implications. Action: SE to outline BYOK flow and legal to draft ed clause.
- Concern raised about prompt caching; we recommended disabling KV cache for PII workflows. Action: implement cache toggle per-route (PR #589) and test.

Open questions / blockers
- BAA signature outstanding; legal kickoff needed.
- Full pen-test PDF redaction for customer distribution (security to confirm redaction plan).
- Evidence transfer mechanism preference from BlueHarbor (S3 share vs artifact portal).

Action items (owner, due)
- Marina: finalize Evidence 01, 02, 03 packets and upload to secure share (due 2026-02-03).
- Devon: coordinate pen-test redaction and secure-sharing process (due 2026-02-14).
- Priya: test per-route cache toggle and validate that disabling KV cache prevents KV persistence (due 2026-02-07).
- Legal: circulate BAA v0.9 with BlueHarbor counsel (due 2026-02-05).

Notes to SEs:
- Keep artifacts minimal; avoid sending full pen-test PDF until BAA in place.
- Record all artifact deliveries in JIRA-ENG-2045 for audit trail.

Appendix: quick artifact delivery checklist
- Compose encrypted zip of Evidence 01-06.
- Create per-artifact manifest with hashes.
- Share via pre-signed S3 links with 7-day expiry and IP restriction where possible.

End of working draft. Comments welcomed on the Evidence index or any required expansions for HIPAA mapping tables.
